title: Sliding window
objective: Find the best run of k neighbours by updating a running sum instead of re-adding.

sources.title: Laaksonen, Competitive Programmer's Handbook: the sliding window method

simplifies: All numbers here are positive and k is fixed. Windows that grow and shrink (for example, "the shortest run with sum at least 20") use the same idea with a moving left edge.

quiz.prompt: Each slide costs how many additions and subtractions, whatever k is?

options.explanation: That is re-adding the whole window. Sliding only adds the new number and removes the old one.
Right. One number in, one out. That is why it is O(n) overall instead of O(n × k).
Only two numbers change as the window moves.

quiz.prompt: With n items and windows of k, how many windows are there?

options.explanation: Right. The first starts at index 0 and the last at index n − k.
Count again: starting positions 0 to n − k is n − k + 1 windows.
Windows near the end would run past the last item.
